extracted.intended_audience: writers and editors of short fiction; readers and contributors to literary magazines
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and editorial standards for selecting, curating, and preparing short stories for a literary anthology — focusing on variety, originality, editorial practice, and permissions. Grounded in an editor's foreword describing selection aims and concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Variety of genres and subject matter
rubrics_metrics.description: "In it they will find a broad cross section of short stories ranging from historical fiction to adventure, from fantasy to problems of contemporary life and love."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An anthology should represent a wide range of forms, modes, and subjects to show the breadth of literary talent; selection should include different genres (historical, adventure, fantasy, contemporary life, love, etc.) so the collection feels representative and varied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intended audience: intelligent readers
rubrics_metrics.description: "THIS BOOK is intended for enjoyment by intelligent readers."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose pieces that provide pleasure and intellectual engagement for thoughtful readers — selections should respect readers' intelligence rather than pander to lowest-common-denominator tastes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve authorial voice; avoid overediting
rubrics_metrics.description: "Another trend seems to be that so much editing of stories is being done that the editors’ hands are becoming too apparent... What they are achieving with all their smoothing out and contriving is about as lifeless and tasteless as most chain-store bread."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial intervention should not erase or 'smooth out' the writer's original voice and communication. Overassiduous revision/re-writing that makes prose lifeless is an anti-pattern; editors should respect authors' expressions and avoid heavy-handed tampering that breaks the writer-reader communication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select for originality and quality
rubrics_metrics.description: "Happily, many good, original short stories are being written and are being published. From them I have chosen this anthology. The original meaning of anthology is 'bouquet.' Some of the stories here may have thorns for some readers but I hope they also find a lot of roses."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize originality and excellence when choosing works; an anthology is a curated bouquet — include pieces that may challenge some readers but that collectively provide aesthetic reward and distinction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wide, informed reading and curation
rubrics_metrics.description: The editor reports having read "the thousands of short stories published during the past year to find those that should go into this collection."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection should be based on broad, thorough reading across publications and levels (pulp to literary quarterlies). Editorial judgments should be informed by exposure to a wide field of contemporary work rather than narrow sampling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obtain permission to reprint
rubrics_metrics.description: GRATEFUL ACKNOWLEDGMENT for permission to reprint the stories in this volume is made to the following: [lists of magazines and authors]. Many stories noted as "Reprinted by permission of..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always secure and acknowledge permission from original publishers/authors before reprinting material in an anthology; proper legal and ethical clearance is required and customary acknowledgments should be included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use knowledgeable readers/assistants for genre coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: The editor thanks David Burnett "especially in regard to fantasy and science fiction," and Joyce Hartman for assistance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When curating across varied genres, consult or employ assistants/readers with subject-matter expertise so genre-specific work (fantasy, SF, etc.) is properly recognized and evaluated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aim to quicken readers' life and pleasure
rubrics_metrics.description: The editor expresses a hope that the anthology "will quicken the life and pleasure of readers whoever and wherever they are, and upset though they may be by whatever stress of today's living."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select stories that move, enliven, or otherwise meaningfully affect readers — emotional and intellectual impact is a desirable selection criterion.
